text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind comes with 10 points of discussion which could be the basis for negotiations.
- Disappointment reigns in right-wing Disy party over election results.
- Rifkind unveils a 10-point proposal for Cyprus
- National Guard missile sales are likely to dominate visit of Turkish foreign Minister Tansu Ciller to Moscow.
- Troubled Cypriots beg to air their problems on Greek social chat show.
- The public approved of the election pact between communist Akel, socialist Edek and the Free Democrats, says Akel leader after election result.
- British decalogue for dialogue and a solution. Rifkind does not say anything new, but is confident of talks in 1997.
- Heads will roll in right-wing Disy party after losses suffered in municipal elections.
- Death of mother of four baffles police.
- Commission investigating alleged irregularities in electricity tender hears conflicting accounts of who received kickbacks.
- Rifkind presents a draft agreement on the Cyprus problem.
- National guardsmen intercept Turkish soldiers who were approaching the government-controlled areas.
